title: Advancing Multimodal Agent Reasoning with Long-Term Neuro-Symbolic Memory

problem.claim: Long-term reasoning is needed for intelligent agents operating in open-world, multimodal environments.

gap.claim: Existing multimodal agent memories primarily use neural representations and vector retrieval, limiting analytical and deductive reasoning needed for real-world decision making.

contributions.claim: NS-Mem is a long-term neuro-symbolic memory framework that integrates neural memory with explicit symbolic structures and rules.

NS-Mem provides a three-layer episodic, semantic, and logic memory architecture; SK-Gen for multimodal knowledge consolidation and incremental updates; and hybrid retrieval combining similarity search with deterministic symbolic queries.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On real-world multimodal reasoning benchmarks, Neuro-Symbolic Memory reportedly improves overall reasoning accuracy by an average of 4.35 percentage points over pure neural memory systems.
The reported gains reach up to 12.5 percentage points on constrained reasoning queries.

narrative_sequence.summary: Intelligent agents are emerging for open-world, multimodal environments, creating a need for long-term reasoning support.
Neural and vector-based multimodal memories are described as inadequate for analytical and deductive reasoning.
NS-Mem integrates neural memory with symbolic structures and rules.
The framework combines layered memory, automated structured-knowledge maintenance, and hybrid retrieval.
The authors report accuracy improvements on multimodal reasoning benchmarks, including constrained reasoning queries.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines similarity-based retrieval with deterministic symbolic query functions.

interpretation.claim: Combining learned representations with explicit symbolic structures may support both intuitive and analytical reasoning.

application.claim: Systems requiring multimodal retrieval and constrained reasoning could consider a hybrid neural-symbolic memory design.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design generalizes beyond the reported benchmarks or reasoning settings.

unknowns: Benchmark names, datasets, baselines, and experimental protocols are not specified.
The abstract does not describe computational costs, failure cases, or ablation results.
Details of SK-Gen's consolidation and update procedures are not provided.
